extracted.intended_audience: general CNBC readers; public interested in business/fashion news and PR/marketing observers
extracted.subtask_description: A news article reporting a fashion house's public apology and removal of an offending product; serves as an example of the elements included in corporate apology statements and crisis PR responses. Useful as a reference for crafting or evaluating apology press releases after public backlash.

rubrics_metrics.name: Expression of remorse / apology
rubrics_metrics.description: "We are deeply sorry for the distress caused by one of the products that featured in our A/W 2019 runway collection," Marco Gobbetti, Burberry's CEO, said in a statement emailed to CNBC.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Clear, unambiguous language of regret (e.g., 'deeply sorry') is used as the lead element of the statement; exemplary wording is shown verbatim.

rubrics_metrics.name: Acknowledge insensitivity and admit mistake
rubrics_metrics.description: "Though the design was inspired by the marine theme that ran throughout the collection, it was insensitive and we made a mistake.","
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Statement both explains context and explicitly labels the action as 'insensitive' and 'a mistake' rather than deflecting blame — model for taking responsibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Explain inspiration or context (without excusing)
rubrics_metrics.description: "While the design was inspired by a nautical theme, I realize that it was insensitive," (Riccardo Tisci).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include concise explanation of intent or design inspiration but avoid using it as a justification; pair explanation with acknowledgement of harm.

rubrics_metrics.name: Immediate corrective action (remove offending item)
rubrics_metrics.description: "It has since been removed from the collection."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Publicly announce concrete remedial steps taken (e.g., removing the product from the collection) to show action beyond words.

rubrics_metrics.name: Senior leadership takes responsibility
rubrics_metrics.description: Statements are issued by CEO Marco Gobbetti and Chief Creative Officer Riccardo Tisci taking responsibility and apologizing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Apologies and commitments should come from senior executives to signal organizational ownership of the issue.

rubrics_metrics.name: Commitment to review and prevent recurrence
rubrics_metrics.description: "We will reflect on this, learn from it, and put in place all necessary actions to ensure it does not happen again."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Promise of internal review and concrete future safeguards is included to reassure stakeholders that steps will be taken to prevent repeat incidents.

rubrics_metrics.name: Acknowledge internal and external criticism
rubrics_metrics.description: Criticism from Liz Kennedy — one of the British fashion house's own models — led to online backlash. Kennedy blasted the brand in an Instagram post ...
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recognize and cite specific criticisms (including those from insiders) rather than ignoring them; demonstrates awareness of stakeholder concerns.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of clear, values-aligned language
rubrics_metrics.description: "It does not reflect my values nor Burberry's and we have removed it from the collection. I will make sure that this does not happen again."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Link apology to company/personal values explicitly to rebuild trust; avoid equivocal language and emphasize alignment with stated values.

rubrics_metrics.name: Public, timely communication through media channels
rubrics_metrics.description: Statements were 'emailed to CNBC' and published quickly after the runway show and ensuing backlash.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Issue prompt, public statements via major media outlets and official channels to ensure wide dissemination and demonstrate responsiveness.
